about: Research record for the two south-pole base-site targets added on 2026-10-14 (mons-mouton, shackleton-ridge) and for the regolith tag rule (VAL9). Every quote below was checked by script to appear in the page or abstract fetched on that date. Temperatures: scripts/extract_diviner.py (data/diviner_malapert.json, base_points; raw windows in data/raw/diviner/). Terrain: scripts/compute_terrain.py with NASA Moon Trek (data/terrain.json; raw responses in data/raw/terrain/mons-mouton.json and shackleton-ridge.json).

sources.usedFor: shackleton-ridge pin (lat -89.46752, lon -138.012788), the 1,937.83 m height and the 'Why here' fact
quotes: Analyzed Shackleton Connecting Ridge (-89.46752, -138.012788 with elevation of 1937.83 meters)
Specific coordinates chosen to match available average seasonal surface temperature flight data from LRO
TLT is a 50-meter-tall tower constructed on the lunar surface near the south pole.
The tower’s height at this location on the moon allows for extended durations of incident solar flux which can be used to generate power via photovoltaic arrays.

quotes: NASA identified the following candidate regions for an Artemis III lunar landing:

Each region is approximately 9.3 by 9.3 miles (15 by 15 kilometers).

massif lithologies and SPA ejecta blankets are not exposed at the surface

checks.ridge_height: LOLA (Moon Trek, 128 ppd, bilinear) at the ridge pin: see data/terrain.json shackleton-ridge.centre_elev_m; NTRS gives 1937.83 m.
checks.ridge_pixel: The NTRS ridge point is 0.1 m from the centre of a 240 m Diviner polar map pixel (data/diviner_malapert.json points_detail.shackleton_ridge), as the NTRS slide says the point was chosen to match LRO temperature data.
checks.ascii_crosscheck: The UCLA server (luna1.diviner.ucla.edu) did not answer on 2026-10-14, so the new pixels are listed in validation.ascii_table_crosscheck.not_checked. The rasters are the same files (same byte sizes) and the Malapert and Shackleton floor pixels give the same values as on 2026-10-09.
